methods.label: Compare lines with a shared entry
methods.explanation:
Two lines with the same sum are especially useful when they share an entry: subtracting that entry leaves equal sums of the other two entries.

The top row and left column both contain \(v\), so
\[
24+w=18+25,
\qquad w=19.
\]
Likewise, the middle column and bottom row both contain \(z\), giving
\[
24+x=25+21,
\qquad x=22.
\]
Now the diagonal containing \(w,x,25\) is completely known. Its sum, and therefore every row and column sum, is
\[
19+22+25=66.
\]
The middle row and bottom row then give
\[
y=66-18-22=26,
\qquad z=66-25-21=20.
\]
Thus \(y+z=26+20=\boxed{46}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
methods.levelReason: Comparing equal sums and solving simple equations uses only elementary arithmetic and school algebra, within AMC 10 scope.

The method needs equation meaning and integer arithmetic, but does not require decimal algorithms or a formal system-solving procedure.
